stem.text: Evaluate the improper integral \( \int_{3}^{\infty} \frac{3 x}{\left(x^{2} + 8\right)^{2}}\,dx \), or show that it diverges.

worked_solution.text: The integral is improper because the upper limit of integration is infinite, so write it as \( \lim_{R\to\infty} \int_{3}^{R} \frac{3 x}{\left(x^{2} + 8\right)^{2}}\,dx \).
Substitute \( u = x^{2} + 8,\ du = 2 x\,dx \). The limits become \( u = 17 \text{ to } u = R^{2} + 8 \), and an antiderivative in u is \( - \frac{3}{2 u} \).
Evaluate the limit: \( \lim_{R\to\infty} \left( - \frac{3}{2 \left(R^{2} + 8\right)} + \frac{3}{34} \right) = \frac{3}{34} \). The limit is finite, so the integral converges to \( \frac{3}{34} \).

options.label: The integral converges to \( \frac{3}{17} \).
options.derivation: the factor 1/2 that du introduces dropped

options.label: The integral converges to \( 1 \).
options.derivation: the original x limits kept after the substitution and the factor 1/2 dropped as well

options.label: The integral converges to \( \frac{1}{2} \).
options.derivation: the original x limits kept after the substitution, the u antiderivative evaluated from u = 3 to infinity
